subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.**

When the District Attorney asked the convict about details of the day of the crime, he started __beating around the bush.__

options.text: Speaking in a confusing manner without giving a correct answer

solution: The correct answer is: **Speaking in a confusing manner without giving a correct answer** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The idiom "B**eating around the bush**" means to treat a topic, but omit its main points, often intentionally; discuss a matter without coming to the point. (घुमा फिराकर बात करना) • Example - *Don't beat around the bush, come straight to the point!* • So, it is clear that the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom "Beating around the bush" is "Speaking in a confusing manner without giving a correct answer" • Hence, the correct answer is option 3. 37:Td2c,
